Cesta semantic interface, version 1

The semantic layer gives a C translation unit its own C meaning: every name is
bound to the entity it denotes and every expression has C11's type for it,
together with its value category and the implicit conversions applied to it.
The AST is unchanged. Each fact is an annotation on an AST node, and the
exports locate nodes by byte extents in the parsed source.

Commands

  cesta bind     [--std=c11|gnu11] [--dialect=gcc|clang] PREPROCESSED-C
  cesta types    [--std=c11|gnu11] [--dialect=gcc|clang] [--abi=ABI] PREPROCESSED-C
  cesta probe    [...same options...] PREPROCESSED-C
  cesta explicit [...same options...] PREPROCESSED-C
  cesta census   [...same options...] PREPROCESSED-C
  cesta abi-tables [--abi=ABI]

bind lists entities and every identifier occurrence that denotes one:
  (entity ID KIND NAME LINKAGE SCOPE DECLARATION-OFFSET)
  (use OFFSET ENTITY ROLE VISIBLE-DECLARATION-OFFSET [folded])
types lists each entity's type, each complete record's layout, and each
expression in tree order:
  (expr BEGIN END "TYPE" CATEGORY [(cast KIND)] (CONVERSION "TO")... [(bits N)] [(value V)] [(folded)])
Types are written as C type names. A conversion is named by the operation it
performs, in the vocabulary C compilers use for implicit casts
(LValueToRValue, ArrayToPointerDecay, IntegralCast, NullToPointer, ...),
in the order the enclosing context applies them.

probe writes the unit back with every typed expression E rewritten as a
generic selection that keeps E's value, type and category and whose never
evaluated controlling expression compares E's type with the elaborated one.
Eligible integer constant expressions of up to 64 bits also compare their
values. Known short-circuit results with nonconstant operands are not included
in that value check. Refusals name the expression's source extent. Record sizes, alignments and
member offsets, and enumeration constants, are asserted after the unit.
explicit writes every conversion that changes representation as a cast to its
target; census classifies what each conversion does to values (preserving,
sign change, narrowing, ...). abi-tables prints the target's integer
promotions and usual arithmetic conversions over all arithmetic types.

Binding

bind, types and census accept --json-lines before --cc. Each line contains the
command and one record as explicitly tagged list, symbol and text atoms.
Valid UTF-8 uses value; other byte strings use hexadecimal bytes. Numeric
spelling remains a symbol, so transport never changes an atom's kind.
Source preprocessing adds original spelling positions and macro expansion
chains to records. Refusals use the same original positions and expansion notes.

Ordinary identifiers follow the profile's scope program: the scope hook data
that classifies typedef names during parsing is executed again over the
tree. The parser and binder therefore use one declared scope policy; their
implementations are independently checked. Tags share those
scopes, labels have function scope, and members are resolved by type during
elaboration. Declarations with linkage denote one entity per translation unit.
Names that compilers predeclare (__builtin_*, __atomic_*, __func__) bind to
builtin entities.

Types and targets

The types are C11's: the standard and extended integer types with plain char
distinct, the standard and TS 18661-3 floating types, complex types,
enumerations, pointers, arrays, functions, structures and unions, with
qualifiers. Typedef names are kept as sugar and never change a type's
identity. Implementation-defined choices belong to a target ABI:

  x86_64-sysv-lp64      the default
  i386-sysv-ilp32
  x86_64-windows-llp64

An ABI gives scalar sizes and alignments, floating formats, the signedness of
char, the types of size_t, ptrdiff_t and wchar_t, and how an enumeration's
integer type is chosen. The System V targets use System V record and bit-field
allocation; the Windows target uses Microsoft's allocation policy. The aligned,
packed and mode attributes participate in layout. The target also determines
the representation of __builtin_va_list.

GCC and Clang read the same GNU C slightly differently, and the dialect
option selects which: Clang reads the TS 18661-3 type names as identifiers,
gives an incremented bit-field the field's declared type where GCC keeps its
width, and spells __PRETTY_FUNCTION__ as the function's signature where GCC
spells its name.

Constraints

Elaboration refuses, at the offending node, the constraint violations that
both GCC and Clang refuse: assignment to a non-modifiable lvalue, use of a
void value, operand and assignment types C does not allow, a call with the
wrong number of arguments, sizeof of an incomplete type, conflicting
declarations of one entity, and the like.

Evidence

The tests check this layer against independent compilers on every corpus
configuration, in both compilers' preprocessing: Clang's AST for binding,
value categories and conversion chains; probes compiled by GCC and by Clang
for types, layouts and constants; Clang's IR for the conversions written as
casts, with value-losing mutations as controls; and GCC's conversion warnings
for the census. The integer promotions and usual arithmetic conversions of all
three targets are kernel-checked against a Lean model of C11's arithmetic
types. These are separate pieces of evidence about this implementation on
these programs; they do not assert a proof of the elaborator.

Boundaries

Inputs are preprocessed C. GNU vector types are refused. Values are folded for
integer constant expressions up to 64 bits.

Qualification

make check runs local native syntax, presentation and semantic controls.
make test retains the corpus, compiler and Lean kernel gates. Completed semantic
units carry content-bound test-evidence receipts: the binary, checker scripts,
compiler tools and libraries, environment, full build command, source and both
preprocessed inputs are checked before reuse. Results are also fingerprinted;
failed results are rechecked. --fresh forces a new corpus run. These receipts
record tests on fixed inputs; they are not universal correctness proofs.
The compiler oracles retain the recorded type/code-generation options; a
selected ABI that disagrees with an option such as -fpack-struct fails layout
qualification.

Explicit-conversion comparisons report raw IR equality separately. Only metadata
referenced as inline-assembly source locations and weaker memory-intrinsic
alignment facts may differ in the normalized comparison. Each alignment change
is recorded; stronger assumptions and changes to instructions, pointers, lengths
or volatility fail the gate. Object equality is reported independently. This
diagnostic rewrite is separate from ordinary presentation compilation, whose
qualification requires matching native objects.
